audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows contradicted the why-text sitting right next to them: whys[0] says 'he owns level 1' while the side read Skill; whys[2] says 'it evens out at 3' while the side read Gnar; whys[4] says 'Level 6 is mine' while the side read Skill; whys[6] says 'late it evens' while the side read Gnar.
audit.why: The packet chart (Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Neeko, Gnar, Skill) agrees with the why-text on every one of those rows, and the mirror flipped its chart as one atomic group to match. The sides were simply never updated.
audit.corrected: Row 0 -> Gnar (3/10), row 2 -> Skill, row 4 -> Neeko (7/10), row 6 -> Skill, each proposed as a full/content pair in one group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was built on 'W-invisibility', which Neeko does not have.
audit.why: Riot's Shapesplitter text is a third-attack proc plus a directional clone; the kit carries no stealth flag. What actually hides the ult is Inherent Glamour — Riot states the Pop Blossom preparation is hidden while disguised. Teaching an invisibility setup gets the player stunned mid-wind-up.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid and wants.you[1] rebuilt on the disguise and the hidden preparation.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Mega Gnar stun is called 'GNAR! (W)' in five places. GNAR! is his R. The Mega W is Wallop; the Mini W is Hyper.
audit.why: Kit file is authority on names, and the two abilities do different things — Wallop is a 7s-cooldown frontal stun, GNAR! is a 90/60/30s throw that only stuns if you hit a wall. Conflating them tells the player to fear the wrong ability and to fight in the wrong place.
audit.corrected: Wallop named as the wind-up interrupt in spikes[2], whys[5], mid and wants.foe[1]; GNAR! named as the wall-stun in late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said that GNAR! denies Neeko's own mobility — Pop Blossom's leap is a dash, and a displacement thrown at you cancels the commit.
audit.why: _missing flags dash-denied for this exact matchup, and the R also creates terrain effects on wall impact.
audit.corrected: Written into late: fight away from terrain, because GNAR! into a wall is a stun on top of the throw.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page kept saying 'track his rage bar like a cooldown' without a single real number for the abilities that punish you.
audit.why: Wallop is a flat 7s, Hop/Crunch is 22s at rank 1 falling to 12s, boomerang is 16s reduced on catch. Those numbers decide whether a step-up is safe.
audit.corrected: Wallop's 7s written into spikes[2], whys[5] and mid.

I can disguise as an ally or pop Shapesplitter (W) to go invisible, set up Pop Blossom unseen, and slam for the stun the instant he's at low Rage and can't transform out. If my E lands first, the root pins mini-Gnar's squishy body and R-into-Q re-bloom is a real kill. The trap is his Rage bar: if he's near full, he transforms mid-fight and mega-Gnar's GNAR! (W) AoE-stuns me out of my channel — so only commit when his Rage is empty.

edits.before: This stays Gnar's matchup. Once he's a ranged poke threat with an item up, his boomerang chunks me from range I can't close, and any fight he enters at high Rage he transforms and CCs my all-in before Pop Blossom lands. My value isn't the 1v1 — it's the teamfight bomb on his team. I never face him alone in a sidelane where his kite and transform timing decide it; I group, land my AoE root on the clustered backline, and use my clone to bait the mega-Gnar GNAR! stun onto a fake. Force 5v5s where his single-target kite matters less than my burst.

notes: The full layer's focus.text, loading, winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0..2] and report[1]/[3]/[5]/[9] all track the threat as 'GNAR! (Mega)'. That is half-right: GNAR! is the ultimate, but the ability those lines actually describe (the thing that punishes a step-up and interrupts the ult) is Wallop, the Mega W. Rewriting them properly means changing the focus token and roughly ten strings that are built around it, which is a larger structural change than a per-string edit can carry inside the length band — worth a targeted pass. Also note the win rate is 33.33% over only 9 games; the difficulty of 5.5/10 and diff EVEN may be understating this lane, but 9 games is too thin to move a rating on, so I left both alone.
